notes: Self-correction inside ONE hermes turn: the user asks for a skill_view of a skill name that does not exist (which comes back success:false), then a skills_list to discover the real names, then a confirming skill_view on a real one — so the single turn carries multiple assistant(finish_reason='tool_calls')→role='tool' round-trips before it settles. The user-observable signal is that state stays continuously working across every retry cycle — no flicker to ready or waiting between the failing attempt and the recovery — and the turn finally settles to ready. This locks down hermes' terminal-finish_reason gate: only an assistant row with finish_reason='stop' closes the turn (parser.go), and Watcher.turnIsDone marks an activity Terminal only for that row, so intermediate tool_calls/tool rows cannot settle the session. The failing tool result is just another role='tool' row and carries no state signal of its own; no hermes tool name is in the user-blocking list (NeedsUserAttention), so no mid-loop waiting is possible either. Hermes writes NO transcript file — the session lives in the shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db, observed by the daemon's ProcessOwnedStore source and keyed by the store's own YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_xxxxxx session id. Like the opencode sibling (the other ProcessOwnedStore adapter), session_birth is anchored to recording start and left UNPINNED so a transient proc-<PID> presession cannot steal identity and cascade same_session_as failures; turn_start establishes the store session identity that turn_end chains off via same_session_as. intermediate_working pins the no-flicker invariant with duration_at_least_ms 3000 — the recipe's three sequential tool round-trips plus the large skills_list payload keep the turn open ~14s, far wider than the store watcher's 2s poll + 500ms debounce, so the working span cannot be coalesced away. The phase DSL has no tool-event form, so the retry cycle itself is asserted via the single sustained working span plus the no-ready/no-waiting invariants; the ≥2 failing-then-recovering tool round-trips are verified out-of-band in state.db at record time. observations assert tokens non-zero only: hermes' sessions row carries populated input_tokens/output_tokens, but cost is deliberately NOT asserted (hermes reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 / billing_mode='subscription_included' and irrlicht reprices via its own alias table, which has no entry for the locally-configured model), and `model` is left unpinned for record to fill from the recording home's config.yaml. RECIPE CORRECTION (record, 2026-08-02): the recipe originally drove hermes' `terminal` tool (`false`, then `sleep 3; echo recovered`). That tool is NOT exposed on this install: config.yaml sets terminal.backend=docker, and with no Docker daemon `terminal`/`process` are filtered out of the function schema, leaving `terminal` only as a TOOLSET name — a prompt naming it yields a turn with zero tool calls, which cannot exercise this cell at all. The failing/recovering pair is now read_file (missing path) -> write_file (create it) -> read_file (confirm), all ungated core file tools. The assertions are unchanged: the cell's claim is about hermes' terminal-finish_reason gate holding `working` across a failing tool round-trip, and that claim is tool-agnostic. RECIPE CORRECTION 2 (record, 2026-08-02): the read_file/write_file rewrite was ALSO wrong, and this was seen live rather than reasoned about — recording attempt 1 produced a turn in which the model, told to "use your file tools", reached for execute_code three times and got "[TOOL_ERROR] ... Docker command is available but 'docker version' failed" every time, never recovering. A tool-roster probe then showed that read_file/write_file/patch/search_files are not in this install's function schema AT ALL (36 callable functions, listed in the recipe's last precondition). The pair is now skill_view (missing name) -> skills_list -> skill_view, verified end to end on a live probe session before re-recording: the first call returns success:false with "Skill 'definitely-not-a-real-skill-xyz' not found.", the recovery lists 68 skills, and the confirming view succeeds. The cell's assertions are unchanged — its claim is that hermes' terminal-finish_reason gate holds `working` across a failing tool round-trip, which is tool-agnostic. UPDATE (record, 2026-08-02): observations.tokens_nonzero REMOVED and `model` pinned in its place. The assessment note above ("observations assert tokens non-zero only ... hermes' sessions row carries populated input_tokens/output_tokens") is wrong about the PATH, not about the store: `of verify` asserts only against the newest recording's replay-golden `summary`, produced by the offline replay tool driving core/pkg/tailer with hermes.Parser, which sets ModelName (and, since 4b65f639, Tasks) and no token vector. The sessions aggregate reaches irrlicht only via ComputeMetrics, which replay never runs, and the store-derived token lift in tools/onboarding-factory/cmd/replay/metrics.go is gated to antigravity. Seen red on this recording (`✗ tokens: want >0 got 0`) with all 4 state phases green. `model` is pinnable because the golden's summary carries model_name — the same removal, same reason, as the committed 2-1 / 1-1 / 2-13 / 2-3 / 1-6 cells.
